description: SGDemTool (Swarm Grid Demand Tool) simulates electricity demand time series for swarm grids. It was released in February 2022 (version 0.1.0) by Jens Weibezahn and used in a paper in Economics of Energy & Environmental Policy on community power purchase agreements for swarm grids. The tool models the use of a set of appliances by different households as a random process, based on survey data on usage times and durations for different weekdays and seasons. Coverage is not tied to a place; inputs come from household surveys. The code is accessible on GitHub and Zenodo under the MIT licence at no cost. Caveats: it is a small single-release tool with little documentation. Simulation uses are demand profiles for sizing off-grid and minigrid systems and market design studies for energy access. Related records: data-india-state-daily-electricity-demand is measured demand at a much larger scale.
inputs: usage times and durations from household surveys
name: SGDemTool - Swarm Grid Demand Tool
